title: Act or ask: Interactive construction robots via vision–language models with confidence-guided decision deferral
task: 自然语言驱动的施工机器人装配与人机协同决策
inputData: 自然语言施工指令 + RGB-D场景图像；SAM分割后以标记关键点作为VLM的中间视觉表征
contribution: 提出Act or Ask施工机器人控制系统，以关键点作为高层语言意图与低层机器人动作之间的中间表征，并通过VLM置信度驱动的decision deferral在低置信度时请求人工决策，实现无需任务微调的共享自主施工装配。
abstract: Act or Ask maps natural-language construction instructions and RGB-D observations to executable robot actions. SAM-based segmentation and marked keypoints form an intermediate representation for GPT-4o visual prompting; confidence from the VLM determines whether the robot acts autonomously or defers to a human. The system is validated on a real Franka Research 3 robot.
methodology: An overhead RGB-D image is segmented with SAM and candidate interaction keypoints are sampled and visually marked. The marked image and a natural-language instruction are supplied to GPT-4o, which selects keypoints specifying the target placement pose. Token-level log-probabilities provide a confidence estimate; low-confidence decisions are deferred to a human supervisor, whereas accepted keypoints are parsed and passed to motion planning and robot execution. The method is tested on a Franka Research 3 arm in wall-truss timber placement, roof-truss timber placement and wall-panel installation tasks without construction-specific VLM fine-tuning.
results: The real-robot experiments report success rates of 60% for wall-truss assembly, 78.5% for roof-truss assembly and 90% for panel installation with decision deferral. In the panel task, disabling deferral reduces success from 90% to 60%; routing low-confidence cases to a human therefore improves successful installation by 30 percentage points. Failure analysis identifies incorrect VLM keypoint selection and segmentation errors as the main residual failure modes.
taskEn: Natural-language-driven construction robot assembly with confidence-guided shared autonomy
inputDataEn: Natural-language construction instructions and RGB-D scene images; SAM-generated marked keypoints serve as the VLM's intermediate visual representation
operationEvidence: The VLM generates target keypoint selections/poses from language and vision, and the accepted decisions are converted into motion plans and physically executed by the robot.
